question: How big is the universe beyond the part that telescopes can ever see?
answer: Nobody knows, but there is a floor. Measurements show space is extremely close to flat, the way a car park looks flat on a round Earth. That flatness means the whole must be far larger than the visible part: one 2011 analysis put it at 251 times the volume or more. It may be infinite.
move: Flat where you stand only proves the whole is very big.
ask: Where am I assuming the world ends at the edge of what I can see?
reference: Vardanyan, Trotta & Silk, Applications of Bayesian model averaging to the curvature and size of the Universe, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society Letters, 2011
